appearance: Egyptian woman about twenty: warm sun-bronzed olive-brown skin, black hair in a thick braid tied with leather, dark almond-shaped eyes, straight nose, lean wiry build; red-ochre lines on her cheekbones. As an old woman: grey braid, deeply lined face, same eyes.
kind: fictional (composite of Western Desert herders, c. 5300 BC)
likeness: bronzed olive-brown Egyptian skin, black braid, almond eyes, ochre lines on cheekbones
name: Nebet
nameNote: Reconstructed name (Egyptian 'nebet', lady). No personal names survive from before writing (c. 3200 BC). Alternatives: Merit, Nefret, Ankhet.
notes: Arc: hunger, loss, terror, faith, rebirth at the river.
summary: Episode 1 narrator. A young herder mother who survives the drought, the lions, the sandstorm and the cave, and reaches the Nile with her baby Wedja. Tells the story years later to her grown son.
voice: quiet, fierce, tender with her son; dry humour; still afraid of storms
wardrobe: goatskin wrap dress tied with a leather cord, ostrich-eggshell bead necklace, leather baby sling across her chest
